newsitem.title: FRANCE: Rebels cut throats of five in Algerian capital-paper.
newsitem.headline: Rebels cut throats of five in Algerian capital-paper.

text.p: Suspected Moslem militants cut the throats of three women and two men, all members of the same family, in the Algerian capital at the weekend, the Algerian newspaper El Watan said on Monday.
It said five or six "terrorists" broke into the house between Bainem and Bouzareah on the heights of Algiers and killed the five.
The family's children managed to flee the house and alert neighbours who arrived too late to save the family.

An hour earlier, the same group had tried to get into a house in the suburb of El Biar but failed. They planted a bomb outside which destroyed part of the house but caused no casualties, the newspaper said.
Bainem forest is a reputed rebel area. Last week, security forces killed two Moslem guerrillas and destroyed five rebel hideouts in the forest, recovering a huge amount of ammunition.

El Watan, giving the latest death toll in an attack on Friday in Douaouada village in the western coastal province of Tipaza said 13 people had been killed. Eight were burnt alive and five had had their throats cut -- the oldest being 75 and the youngest a baby girl of two.
It said four more people had been killed on the Chenoua seafront area in Tipaza, and another civilian had been hit by two bullets in the throat. It gave no other details.
The reported attacks were the latest in a series of killings which the authorities blame on Moslem guerrillas trying to topple them.

More than 90 villagers were slaughtered by Moslem guerrillas last month in the worst massacre in five-and-a-half years of violence following the cancellation of the last general election in which Moslem fundamentalists had taken a commanding lead.
About 60,000 people have died in the violence.
